intended_object: The transport derivative (b·∇)e = Σ_i b_i ∂_i e of a vector field e (values in ℝ^q) along a velocity field b on the cylinder ℝ³ × ℝ/(period·ℤ). The four coordinates are ordered with the angle first. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the H⁶ transport-source estimates in the file.
explanation: The body is Σ_{i:Fin 4} b(x)_i • fieldDerivative (standardDirection i) e x. Here fieldDerivative is the Fréchet derivative at 0, in the given direction, of the local lift h ↦ e(x.1+h.1, x.2+h.2) from the covering tangent space ℝ³×ℝ. So it is the genuine directional derivative on the cylinder. standardDirection i = coordinateEquiv (e_i), and coordinateEquiv puts coordinate 0 on the circle factor and coordinates 1–3 on ℝ³. This matches the docstring's "angle is the first coordinate" and the coordinate ordering of b. By linearity of the derivative in the direction, the sum equals fderiv(lift e)(0)(coordinateEquiv (b x)), which is exactly (b·∇)e and agrees with the library's general fieldTransport. The operator is specific to this library's cylinder setting, and its content (local lift, coordinate convention) needs that setting, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no transport-operator counterpart beyond fderiv itself.
